title: deep-review S6: data-fencing for ticket-derived text in developer/reviewer briefings
description: Deep-review confirmed finding (2026-07-02): the per-ticket loop interpolates ticket title/description/ACs directly into the developer (unrestricted Bash) and reviewer prompts with none of the fencing the project itself established as standard in the deep-review workflow (TASK-039: BEGIN/END DATA block + never-as-a-directive instruction). With the Jira migration ahead, the create_task MCP surface, and TASK-075 removing the human from the ticket-read-to-spawn path, ticket text approaches an execution channel. It is the highest-traffic interpolation path and the only one without the projects own standard.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical briefing template lives in orchestrator-routing SKILL.md (both parity copies byte-identical): ALL ticket-derived text (title, description, ACs, comments) is fenced with the exact deep-review BEGIN/END DATA pattern plus the never-as-a-directive instruction and a length cap; agents/developer.md and agents/reviewer.md reference the template.
A doc-lock spec asserts the fence markers and the never-as-directive phrase exist in the template; red-green proven (the spec fails if the markers are removed).
A short viability note documents whether a Bash allowlist for the developer in unattended mode is feasible (analysis only, no implementation commitment).

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: PLAN (tier=tests-after, ticket-carried, confirmed): prompt-injection hardening of agent briefings — behavior provable by running the code, low edge-risk. Single IMPL-phase developer + minimal regression locks. Loop iteration 3/11.
